en.title: Modern Warfare 4 Nuke Calling Card Now Impossible After Patch
en.summary: A recent update to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has sparked player outrage by making it impossible to earn the coveted "Ground Zero" Calling Card in Free-for-All matches. The change, intended to curb boosting, has inadvertently locked out legitimate players from a long-standing challenge.
en.body:
The pursuit of prestige in **Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4** has hit a significant roadblock for many dedicated players. A recent patch introduced by developer **Infinity Ward** has effectively made it impossible to unlock the "Ground Zero" Calling Card, a cosmetic reward that requires earning a tactical nuke killstreak in a Free-for-All match. This change has ignited a firestorm of frustration within the game's community, who feel their efforts and in-game achievements are being devalued.

The core of the issue lies in two key adjustments **Infinity Ward** made to the Free-for-All mode: a reduction in the required score to win and a change to party size limits. Previously, players needed 30 kills to win a Free-for-All match. To achieve a tactical nuke, a player must secure 30 consecutive kills without dying. The new patch lowered the win requirement to 25 kills. While seemingly a minor adjustment, this change, combined with the party size limit now restricting players to entering with only one friend, has created a scenario where the 30-kill requirement for a nuke is virtually unattainable within the shortened match duration.

## The Fallout for Dedicated Players

The "Ground Zero" Calling Card has long been a symbol of exceptional skill and dedication in **Modern Warfare 4**. Players who have spent countless hours honing their abilities in Free-for-All were working towards this ultimate reward. The patch, while ostensibly aimed at preventing "account boosting" – a practice where players team up to farm kills for each other – has had the unintended consequence of punishing legitimate players. Many fans expressed their disappointment online, with one player lamenting, “One of the calling cards is literally 30 kills in a FFA match lmao brain dead.” Another commented, “Can we not keep changing stuff? FFA has always been 30 kills why change it now?” The sentiment across the community appears overwhelmingly negative, with players feeling that **Infinity Ward** has failed to consider the impact of their changes on the core player base.

## What's Next

As of now, **Infinity Ward** has not announced any plans to revert these changes or adjust the requirements for the "Ground Zero" Calling Card. Players are left hoping for a future update that addresses this oversight, either by restoring the original win condition for Free-for-All or by modifying the Calling Card's unlock criteria to something achievable within the current game parameters. Until then, the ultimate Free-for-All challenge remains out of reach.

content_raw: A new patch for Modern Warfare 4 has players up in arms because it prevents you from getting a tactical nuke Killstreak in Free-for-All, one of the Multiplayer modes. “We've made two adjustments to Free-for-All in #MW4,” developer Infinity Ward announced in a tweet , which included confirmation of a score reduction and a party size change. Now, you can only enter Free-For-All matches with one friend in your party. On top of that, the score required to win a Free-For-All match has been reduced to 25 kills. It was previously 30 kills. Players are upset because this change locks them out of 100% completing the game. A Calling Card called Ground Zero requires players to earn a tactical nuke in a Free-For-All match, but the new score cap prevents this from being possible, since you need to earn 30 consecutive kills without dying to get a nuke. There’s no word on whether Activision and Infinity Ward plan to reduce the requirement for a nuke in Free-For-All or change the Calling Card to something that’s, you know, possible. These changes come to the game after an uptick in account boosting in Free-For-All. Players who wanted to earn the Ground Zero Calling Card were coming in with three friends and farming each other to earn the nuke, essentially ruining the game for everyone else. Obviously, these changes should put an end to that, but it’s annoying for players who wanted to play Free-For-All legitimately with their friends, or earn the Calling Card the right way. “One of the calling cards is literally 30kills in a FFA match lmao brain dead,” said one player . “Can we not keep changing stuff? FFA has always been 30 kills why change it now?” asked another . Sentiment is almost entirely negative in the replies to the announcement so it won’t be a huge surprise if Infinity Ward reverses the decision or at least tweaks it in some way. This news landed just after Shipment, one of Call of Duty’s most iconic maps, was added to Modern Warfare 4 .
